articles.title: ‘Women are not victims’: Türk calls for women to be at the heart of peace and security
articles.summary: Women must be at the centre of efforts to prevent conflict and build lasting peace, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said on Thursday.
articles.content:
He warned that women and girls continue to suffer disproportionate harm in conflicts, while often being excluded from decisions affecting their security.

Addressing the International Civil Society Action Network’s 2026 Forum on Women, Peace and Security in The Hague in a video message, Mr. Türk said the world was experiencing “seismic global shocks”, with conflicts affecting millions of people.

According to latest data looking at 2024, an estimated 676 million women and girls lived within 50 kilometers of active conflict, the highest figure recorded since the end of the Cold War.

“Women are the overwhelming majority of victims of conflict-related rape, abductions, human trafficking, and sexual slavery,” he said.

He stressed that discrimination can increase women’s exposure to harm, particularly when conflict erupts.

Risks rise without investment

“The lower the resources allocated to women – in terms of health, wealth and education – the greater their exposure to harm,” he said.

Women and girls from racially and ethnically marginalised groups, as well as those facing discrimination on religious or other grounds, can be particularly vulnerable, including to sexual violence, he added.

Mr. Türk also pointed to what he described as a persistent gap between the role women play in protecting communities and their representation in formal decision-making.

‘Women are not victims’

While recognising the disproportionate impact of conflict on women and girls, the High Commissioner rejected the idea of portraying women solely as victims.

“But women are not victims,” he said. “On the contrary: all over the world, even in the harshest and most violent environments, women continue to lead, organise, mediate, and document violations.”

Women are often among the first to respond to humanitarian crises, he said, drawing on knowledge of local conditions that international organisations may lack.

Stressing the crucial role women have in preventing conflict, Mr. Türk added that “they are very powerful builders of community protection, accountability, and peace.”

Rethinking security

The High Commissioner argued that lasting peace cannot be built in societies marked by discrimination and oppression, and called for greater recognition of women-led civil society organisations as full partners.

He also called for a broader understanding of what constitutes security.

“Equality; impartial institutions for policing and accountability; economic and social justice; non-violent mediation; and governance that fulfils people's human rights make a society far more safe than spiralling military budgets that choke off spending for essential services,” he said.

For Mr. Türk, protecting human rights is also a means of strengthening societies against future crises.

“Upholding human rights is an investment in enduring social cohesion,” he said. “It builds societies that are resilient to shocks, because they are fair.”

He called for women’s equal participation in decisions affecting their communities and countries: “Gender equality is not a favour that men are doing to women. It is fundamental to humanity, and benefits everyone,” he said.

Supporting women peacebuilders

The UN human rights office (OHCHR) is working with women rights defenders and seeking to expand their access to international mechanisms.

Mr. Türk cited support for accountability for conflict-related sexual violence in countries including Colombia, Sudan and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as support for women mediators and leaders across Africa.

articles.personality_title: UN calls for women to lead peace and security efforts worldwide
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Conflicts around the world continue to harm millions, especially women and girls, who often face violence and are excluded from important decisions about their safety.

**What happened** – On Thursday, Volker Türk, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, spoke at an international forum in The Hague. He urged that women must be at the center of efforts to prevent conflicts and build lasting peace. He shared new data showing that in 2024, 676 million women and girls lived near active conflicts, the highest number since the Cold War ended.

**Impact** – Türk highlighted that women are often the main victims of war crimes like rape and human trafficking. Yet, they are also leaders who help protect communities and work for peace, even in dangerous places. He explained that when women have fewer resources like education and healthcare, they face greater risks during conflicts. He also pointed out that lasting peace needs fair treatment, justice, and equal participation for women, not just more military spending.

**What's next step** – The UN’s human rights office is supporting women peacebuilders in countries such as Colombia, Sudan, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. They are helping women defenders get more access to international support and encouraging governments to include women in peace talks and decisions.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The UN urges that empowering women as leaders and decision-makers is essential to building safer, fairer communities and lasting peace worldwide.
articles.personality_title_fr: L’ONU appelle à mettre les femmes au cœur des efforts de paix et de sécurité
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les conflits mondiaux continuent de toucher des millions de personnes, en particulier les femmes et les filles, qui subissent souvent des violences et sont exclues des décisions importantes concernant leur sécurité.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Jeudi, Volker Türk, Haut-Commissaire des Nations unies aux droits de l’homme, a pris la parole lors d’un forum international à La Haye. Il a insisté sur le fait que les femmes doivent être au centre des efforts pour prévenir les conflits et construire une paix durable. Il a présenté des données montrant qu’en 2024, 676 millions de femmes et filles vivaient près de zones de conflit actif, un chiffre record depuis la fin de la guerre froide.

**Impact** – M. Türk a souligné que les femmes sont souvent les principales victimes de crimes de guerre comme les viols et la traite humaine. Pourtant, elles sont aussi des leaders qui protègent leurs communautés et œuvrent pour la paix, même dans des environnements dangereux. Il a expliqué que le manque de ressources telles que l’éducation ou la santé augmente les risques pour les femmes en temps de conflit. Il a aussi rappelé qu’une paix durable nécessite un traitement équitable, la justice et la participation égale des femmes, pas seulement plus de dépenses militaires.

**Prochaine étape** – Le bureau des droits de l’homme de l’ONU soutient les femmes bâtisseuses de paix en Colombie, au Soudan et en République démocratique du Congo. Il aide les défenseures des droits à accéder davantage aux mécanismes internationaux et encourage les gouvernements à inclure les femmes dans les négociations et décisions de paix.

**Une phrase clé** – L’ONU affirme que donner aux femmes un rôle de leader et de décisionnaire est essentiel pour bâtir des communautés plus sûres, justes et une paix durable dans le monde entier.
articles.personality_title_es: ONU pide que las mujeres lideren los esfuerzos de paz y seguridad en el mundo
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los conflictos en todo el mundo continúan afectando a millones, especialmente a mujeres y niñas, quienes a menudo sufren violencia y son excluidas de decisiones importantes sobre su seguridad.

**Qué pasó** – El jueves, Volker Türk, Alto Comisionado de las Naciones Unidas para los Derechos Humanos, habló en un foro internacional en La Haya. Instó a que las mujeres estén en el centro de los esfuerzos para prevenir conflictos y construir una paz duradera. Compartió datos que muestran que en 2024, 676 millones de mujeres y niñas vivían cerca de conflictos activos, la cifra más alta desde el fin de la Guerra Fría.

**Impacto** – Türk destacó que las mujeres son a menudo las principales víctimas de crímenes de guerra como violaciones y trata de personas. Sin embargo, también son líderes que protegen sus comunidades y trabajan por la paz, incluso en lugares peligrosos. Explicó que cuando las mujeres tienen menos recursos como educación y salud, enfrentan mayores riesgos durante los conflictos. Además, señaló que la paz duradera requiere un trato justo, justicia y participación igualitaria para las mujeres, no solo más gastos militares.

**Próximo paso** – La oficina de derechos humanos de la ONU está apoyando a mujeres constructoras de paz en países como Colombia, Sudán y la República Democrática del Congo. Están ayudando a defensoras de derechos a acceder a más apoyo internacional y animando a los gobiernos a incluir a las mujeres en las negociaciones y decisiones de paz.

**Una frase clave** – La ONU pide que empoderar a las mujeres como líderes y tomadoras de decisiones es clave para construir comunidades más seguras, justas y una paz duradera en todo el mundo.

articles.title: No more execution attempts on Christa Pike: UN rights chief
articles.summary: The UN human rights chief and nine independent rights experts on Thursday called on authorities in Tennessee not to pursue any further attempts to execute Christa Pike, saying her case highlights multiple concerns surrounding the death penalty.
articles.content:
What you need to know

Ms. Pike was denied clemency and, one hour before her execution, a court halted it then lifted the stay

She was twice injected with lethal drugs and survived

Calls are growing for authorities to commute Ms. Pike’s death sentence

“The prolonged suffering – physical and mental – arising from multiple failed execution attempts is abhorrent and cruel,” Volker Türk said in a statement.

Tweet URL

The UN rights chief pointed to unresolved questions surrounding Ms. Pike’s fair trial, saying they raised additional concerns about proceeding with another execution attempt.

The statement comes amid what the UN office described as an increase in the number of executions in the United States, with the Pike case renewing attention to the human rights implications of capital punishment in the country, including safeguards for fair trials and the treatment of people subjected to repeated execution attempts.
articles.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
articles.reasoning: The article reports a significant human rights intervention where the UN rights chief and experts call to halt further execution attempts on Christa Pike, highlighting concerns about the death penalty's fairness and cruelty. This has broad societal implications regarding capital punishment and human rights protections in the US, with detailed context on the case and its impact.
articles.personality_title: UN calls to stop further execution attempts on Christa Pike over human rights concerns
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Christa Pike is a woman on death row in Tennessee, USA. Recently, she survived two attempts to execute her with lethal drugs. Her case has raised questions about the fairness and treatment of people sentenced to death.

**What happened** – In 2024, Ms. Pike was denied clemency, meaning she was not forgiven or given a lighter sentence. Just one hour before her scheduled execution, a court stopped it but then allowed the execution to proceed. Despite being injected twice with lethal drugs, she survived both times. This unusual situation led to calls from the United Nations (UN) and independent rights experts to stop any more attempts to execute her.

**Impact** – The UN human rights chief, Volker Türk, said the repeated attempts caused Ms. Pike to suffer both physically and mentally, which he called cruel. The case also highlights concerns about whether Ms. Pike had a fair trial before being sentenced to death. This situation has brought attention to how the death penalty is used in the United States, especially when executions fail or when there are questions about legal fairness.

**What's next step** – The UN and rights experts want Tennessee authorities to stop trying to execute Ms. Pike again. Her case may encourage more discussions about changing the death penalty laws in the US, improving legal protections, and considering alternatives to capital punishment.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The UN urges Tennessee to halt further execution attempts on Christa Pike, spotlighting important human rights questions about the death penalty’s fairness and treatment of prisoners.
articles.personality_title_fr: L’ONU demande d’arrêter les nouvelles tentatives d’exécution de Christa Pike pour des raisons de droits humains
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Christa Pike est une femme dans le couloir de la mort au Tennessee, aux États-Unis. Récemment, elle a survécu à deux tentatives d’exécution par injection létale. Son cas soulève des questions sur l’équité et le traitement des personnes condamnées à mort.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – En 2024, Mme Pike s’est vu refuser la clémence, ce qui signifie qu’elle n’a pas été graciée ni vue sa peine allégée. Une heure avant son exécution prévue, un tribunal a d’abord suspendu l’exécution, puis l’a autorisée à continuer. Malgré deux injections de drogues létales, elle a survécu aux deux tentatives. Cette situation inhabituelle a conduit l’ONU et des experts indépendants en droits humains à demander l’arrêt de toute nouvelle tentative d’exécution.

**Impact** – Le chef des droits humains de l’ONU, Volker Türk, a déclaré que ces tentatives répétées ont causé à Mme Pike des souffrances physiques et mentales, qualifiées de cruelles. Le cas met aussi en lumière des doutes sur la justice de son procès. Cette affaire attire l’attention sur l’utilisation de la peine de mort aux États-Unis, surtout quand les exécutions échouent ou que des questions légales restent sans réponse.

**Prochaine étape** – L’ONU et les experts demandent aux autorités du Tennessee d’arrêter les nouvelles tentatives d’exécution. Ce cas pourrait encourager des discussions sur la modification des lois sur la peine de mort aux États-Unis, l’amélioration des protections juridiques et la recherche d’alternatives à la peine capitale.

**Phrase clé** – L’ONU presse le Tennessee de cesser les tentatives d’exécution de Christa Pike, mettant en lumière des questions importantes sur les droits humains liées à l’équité de la peine de mort et au traitement des prisonniers.
articles.personality_title_es: ONU pide detener más intentos de ejecución de Christa Pike por preocupaciones de derechos humanos
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Christa Pike es una mujer condenada a muerte en Tennessee, EE. UU. Recientemente, sobrevivió dos intentos de ejecución con inyecciones letales. Su caso ha generado dudas sobre la justicia y el trato hacia personas sentenciadas a muerte.

**Qué pasó** – En 2024, a la señora Pike se le negó el indulto, lo que significa que no le perdonaron ni redujeron su condena. Una hora antes de su ejecución programada, un tribunal la detuvo, pero luego permitió que continuara. A pesar de recibir dos inyecciones letales, sobrevivió a ambos intentos. Esta situación poco común llevó a que la ONU y expertos independientes pidieran que no se realicen más intentos para ejecutarla.

**Impacto** – El jefe de derechos humanos de la ONU, Volker Türk, dijo que los intentos repetidos le causaron sufrimiento físico y mental, calificándolo de cruel. El caso también resalta preocupaciones sobre si tuvo un juicio justo antes de ser condenada a muerte. Esto ha llamado la atención sobre el uso de la pena de muerte en Estados Unidos, especialmente cuando las ejecuciones fallan o hay dudas legales.

**Próximo paso** – La ONU y expertos quieren que las autoridades de Tennessee detengan más intentos de ejecución contra Pike. Su caso podría impulsar debates para cambiar las leyes de la pena de muerte, mejorar las protecciones legales y buscar alternativas a la pena capital.

**Frase clave** – La ONU insta a Tennessee a detener más intentos de ejecución de Christa Pike, destacando importantes preguntas sobre los derechos humanos y la justicia en la pena de muerte.
